                                     PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT LARGE              §           PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LOAD INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS             §
 UNDER PURA 37.0561                         §                     OF TEXAS


               COMMENTS OF CENTERPOINT ENERGY HOUSTON ELECTRIC, LLC

       CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, LLC (“CenterPoint Energy” or the “Company”)

submits these comments on the Staﬀ Discussion Draft of a proposed new rule to be codiﬁed at

16 Tex. Admin. Code (TAC) § 25.194, which was ﬁled in this project on December 1, 2025, to

implement PURA § 37.0561 as enacted by SB 6 during the 2025 legislative session. PURA §

37.0561 requires the Commission to establish standards for interconnecting large load customers

in the ERCOT power region. The Company appreciates Commission Staﬀ’s Discussion Draft. The

Company however oﬀers a revised and reworked alternative rule 25.194 proposal for

consideration to implement PURA § 37.0561 as an attachment to these comments. In the

following comments, CenterPoint Energy oﬀers an explanation of how the large load customer

interconnection process would work under its proposed alternative rule in accordance with PURA

§ 37.0561. CenterPoint Energy ﬁrst responds to speciﬁc questions in Staﬀ’s Discussion Draft.

                                  Discussion Draft Questions

1.    Should the commission deﬁne parameters for determining whether a large load
customer is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request? If so, how should the
commission deﬁne those parameters?

       CenterPoint Energy is unable to identify any objective parameters that the Commission

can use for determining if a large load customer is pursuing a substantially similar request for

service, the approval of which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or




                                                1
 withdrawing its interconnection request. The Commission must instead rely on the large load

customer’s own, subjective disclosure on this question.

2.      Proposed subsections (c)(3), (e)(3), and (h)(3) require the disclosure of speciﬁc
information related to a substantially similar request for interconnection and allows a large
load customer to anonymize competitively sensitive details. Should the commission list what is
and is not competitively sensitive (e.g., load zone is not competitively sensitive information)?
If so, what information should and should not be considered competitively sensitive such that
the interconnecting utility and ERCOT can identify whether there is a duplicate request, or a
request is unlikely to materialize?

         CenterPoint Energy is unable to identify any material beneﬁts to be derived from listing

the types of information that should be considered competitively sensitive. The designation of

competitively sensitive information should be determined in good faith by the large load

customer making the disclosure. As an interconnecting electric utility, CenterPoint Energy will

treat all information received from a large load customer requesting interconnection for which

the customer expressly requests not be disclosed as proprietary customer information in

accordance with 16 TAC § 25.272(c)(5). 1

3.      Should the commission require a large load customer to notify the interconnecting
electric utility and ERCOT of any change to information that is initially disclosed in response to
this rule or only material changes to the information disclosed? If only material changes, how
should "material change" be deﬁned?

         CenterPoint Energy believes the rule to be adopted in this Project should require a large

load customer to update the information initially disclosed in its interconnection request for any




1
  16 TAC § 25.272(c)(5), the Commission’s Code of Conduct rule, deﬁnes proprietary customer information as
including not only “electricity usage” information and “individual contract terms and conditions,” but also “any other
information that the customer has expressly requested not be disclosed.” Subsection (g)(1) of that rule prohibits a
utility from releasing any proprietary customer information to any entity, subject to certain exceptions stated in that
subsection. PURA § 37.0561(d)’s directive to the Commission to adopt a rule that would prohibit an electric utility
“from selling, sharing, or disclosing information submitted to the utility” other than a disclosure to the Commission
or to ERCOT has already been fulﬁlled by the Commission’s Code of Conduct rule.

                                                          2
 changes in that information that arise after the submission of the interconnection request. This

would eliminate any ambiguity as to whether the change is material or not.

4.      Proposed subsection (k)(1) authorizes an interconnecting electric utility to refund 20%
of a large load customer’s security after energization and ratably as the large load customer
meets the milestones identiﬁed in the customer’s schedule for phased energization of its
contracted load. Should the commission standardize the rate for refund for reaching milestones
identiﬁed in the customer's schedule for phased energization (e.g., 20% for each year of
operations until the full amount of security is refunded)? If so, how should the commission
standardize the refund?

       Proposed substation (k) of the Discussion Draft would allow the interconnecting electric

utility to retain 80% of the ﬁnancial security provided by a large load customer until the customer

has achieved ﬁve years of sustained operation at the contracted peak demand. The other 20% of

the ﬁnancial security could be returned “ratably” prior to the end of that ﬁve-year period based

on the customer achieving the milestones identiﬁed in a phased energization schedule that would

be part of the interconnection agreement. The rate of the refund for this 20% could be based on

the percentage of the total contracted peak demand that each milestone represents. However,

if there is no phased energization schedule (i.e., the customer’s contracted peak demand load is

intended to be fully operational upon energization), then CenterPoint Energy interprets this

subsection as requiring 100% of the ﬁnancial security to be retained by the utility until the

subsection (k)(2), ﬁve-year refund trigger is met.

5.    Are changes to the commission's other substantive rules necessary to align with this
rulemaking? If so, what changes need to be made to which rules?

       CenterPoint Energy believes it would be helpful, and would avoid confusion, if the

Commission updates the pro forma Retail Delivery Tariﬀ that is part of the Commission’s rules at

16 TAC § 25.214(d), to incorporate the large load interconnection process that is ultimately

adopted in this Project No. 58481. Section 5.3.1.2 of the current pro forma Retail Delivery Tariﬀ

                                                 3
 states: “Where Construction Services are required prior to the initiation of Delivery System

Service, Retail Customer may contact Company directly to make arrangements for such service.

All such requests shall be governed by the provisions in Section 5.7, FACILITIES EXTENSION

POLICY.” (Emphasis added). Section 5.7 of the pro forma Retail Delivery Tariﬀ should be updated

to reﬂect the facilities extension policy changes adopted by the Commission in this Project to

implement PURA § 37.0561. Since those tariﬀ provisions are part of the Commission’s substantive

rules adopted in 16 TAC § 25.214(d), the only way to make the necessary conforming changes is

through a rulemaking project.

       CenterPoint Energy also believes it could be helpful to revise the Commission’s rate ﬁling

package (the “RFP”) adopted under the Commission’s rules at 16 TAC § 22.243(b). In Project No.

49199, the Commission revised the RFP to add Schedule M: Certain Plant Additions. Speciﬁcally,

RFP Schedule M-3.2 was added, which requires investor-owned utilities to include transmission

projects for which a contribution in aid of construction (“CIAC”) was required. It requires the

utility to state the total cost of the project, the amount of that total that was directly charged to

a customer as CIAC, and the amount of that total that is requested to be included in rate base.

The Company believes it would be helpful for Commission Staﬀ’s review of these costs in a

ratemaking proceeding to split RFP Schedule M-3.2 into two parts: one part for only large load

customer interconnection projects for which a customer CIAC was required, and a second part

for all other transmission projects for which a customer CIAC was required.

                                   Discussion Draft Comments

       For ratemaking purposes, there are two general categories of interconnection costs

incurred by an electric utility to interconnect a load customer. First, there are the “Direct Costs,”


                                                 4
 which are the costs incurred by an electric utility to purchase and construct the new transmission

facilities that are necessary to deliver power from the ERCOT transmission system to the

interconnecting load customer and that will be used by the electric utility, at least initially, to

provide power delivery service exclusively to the interconnecting load customer (the “Load

Interconnection Facilities”). Second, there are the “Upgrade Costs,” which are the costs incurred

by an electric utility to install or upgrade certain equipment on the existing transmission system

to ensure that the reliability of the existing transmission system is maintained and not

compromised with the addition of the interconnecting load customer (the “Upgrade Facilities”).

         The entire amount of the Direct Costs should be paid by the interconnecting load

customer as a CIAC, 2 unless the electric utility’s construction services policy in its Commission-

approved tariﬀ provides an interconnection allowance to oﬀset all or some of the interconnecting

load customer’s Direct Cost responsibility.3 The reason for placing responsibility for Direct Costs

on the interconnecting load customer is that the Load Interconnection Facilities only beneﬁt the




2
  An electric utility may require an interconnecting load customer to pay the CIAC upfront, before the electric utility
incurs any Direct Costs, in which case the amount of the upfront CIAC will be based on the electric utility’s good faith
estimate of the Direct Costs, subject to a true-up to actual costs after the construction of the Load Interconnection
Facilities is completed. Alternatively, an electric utility may require the interconnecting load customer to pay the
CIAC after the construction of the Load Interconnection Facilities is completed, in which case the amount of the CIAC
will be based on the actual cost of Load Interconnection Facilities. In that case, where the CIAC is be paid after the
construction of the Load Interconnection Facilities is completed, the electric utility may require the interconnecting
load customer to provide a ﬁnancial security (e.g., a bank letter of credit) upfront, before the electric utility incurs
any Direct Costs, in an amount based on the electric utility’s good faith estimate of the Direct Costs, to secure the
interconnecting load customer’s obligation to pay the CIAC after the construction of the Load Interconnection
Facilities is completed.
3
  CenterPoint Energy’s construction services policy in its Commission-approved tariﬀ provides an interconnection
allowance (referred to therein as a “facilities extension allowance”) for new distribution-voltage load customer
interconnections, but it expressly excludes an interconnection allowance for new transmission-voltage load customer
interconnections. In the future, the Company may seek Commission approval to extend an interconnection
allowance for new transmission-voltage load customer interconnections to cover at least some of the
interconnection Direct Costs.

                                                           5
 interconnecting load customer. 4 Direct Costs, in other words, are non-rate base-eligible costs, as

that term is used in the Company’s Alternative Proposed Rule attached to these comments. 5

         Upgrade Costs, however, are rate base-eligible costs, as that term is used in the Company’s

Alternative Proposed Rule. Since Upgrade Facilities beneﬁt all transmission service customers

who use the transmission system by maintaining the transmission system’s reliability, the

Upgrade Facilities should be deemed used and useful for the provision of transmission service to

the public. The electric utility that incurs the Upgrade Costs, therefore, should be allowed to

include those costs in its transmission system rate base for recovery through rates.

         An interconnecting load customer should be obligated to pay the Upgrade Costs only if (1)

the interconnecting load customer cancels the load interconnection project after the electric

utility has incurred Upgrade Costs, or (2) the Commission disallows the Upgrade Costs from

recovery in rate base in a ratemaking proceeding in which the electric utility’s Upgrade Costs were

included in its rate ﬁling packages. 6 To secure this obligation to pay to pay the Upgrade Costs if

either of those events occurs, the electric utility should be able to require the interconnecting

load customer to provide it with a ﬁnancial security upfront before the electric utility incurs any

Upgrade Costs. The Company’s Alternative Proposed Rule attached to these comments does this.




4
 If the Load Interconnection Facilities are later used to also interconnect one or more other individual load customers
directly to the ERCOT transmission system, then the Company would support a requirement to allocate the Direct
Cost responsibility for the Load Interconnection Facilities among all such load customers.
5
 However, if the Load Interconnection Facilities are later used to directly interconnect a distribution substation used
by the electric utility to deliver power to load customers on the electric utility’s distribution system, then the Direct
Costs of those Load Interconnection Facilities may become rate base-eligible costs (since those facilities would then
become used and useful for providing delivery service to the public), in which case the Company would support a
requirement to refund the CIAC collected for those facilities and move their costs to rate base for recovery.
6
 The Commission may disallow capital projects from rate base recovery for various reasons, such as by ﬁnding that
the Upgrade Costs were not prudently incurred, or that the Upgrade Facilities themselves were not used and useful.

                                                           6
        The Company is concerned that the Discussion Draft’s requirements for a discretionary

services agreement in 25.194(e) and an intermediate agreement in 25.194(f), and their diﬀering

ﬁnancial security descriptions, are confusing and could have the unintended consequences of

creating barriers and costly delays for load customers seeking to eﬃciently interconnect to the

ERCOT gird. The Company appreciates Staﬀ’s eﬀort to balance an eﬃcient interconnection

request process against the need for greater certainty in the large load interconnection process

but is concerned that the current Discussion Draft’s overly prescriptive requirements for how the

large load interconnection study requirements may conﬂict with the large load interconnection

study process and procedures adopted by ERCOT in Planning Guide Section 9. CenterPoint

Energy’s alternative proposal for 16 TAC § 25.194 seeks to harmonize the Company’s large load

experience and the large load interconnection process in a manner that is consistent with PURA

§ 37.0561, and in a way that provides greater certainty in the current dynamic interconnection

environment while allowing for eﬃcient interconnections for large load customers that want to

connect with the ERCOT grid.

       A.     Interconnection Agreements

       The Discussion Draft requires two new separate agreements, neither of which resemble

the actual interconnection agreements that the Company has historically used for large load

customer interconnections to the ERCOT transmission system. First, it would require the

interconnecting electric utility and the large load customer to execute a discretionary services

agreement, and the large load customer to provide a ﬁnancial security on a per MW basis, before

the commencement of a large load interconnection study.




                                               7
         The Discussion Draft also requires the interconnecting electric utility and the large load

customer to execute a second agreement, called an intermediate agreement, with both a

ﬁnancial security and CIAC requirement, no later than 180 days after the completion of the large

load interconnection study, but with the ﬁnancial security limited exclusively to the procurement

costs of long lead-time equipment. CenterPoint Energy sees no reason or beneﬁt in requiring a

discretionary services agreement with a ﬁnancial security commitment before a large load

interconnection study is even commenced. The Company understands Staﬀ's proposal but

believes that these additional requirements may create unnecessary barriers to interconnect to

the ERCOT grid, and that these requirements could be covered in the utility’s standard

interconnection agreement if that is the policy the Commission adopts.7

        B.       Financial Security and CIAC

        The ﬁnancial commitment required by PURA § 37.0561(h) can be either a “security” or a

“contribution in aid of construction” or CIAC. As set out in the Company’s proposed alternative

rule 25.194, (1) a security (or ﬁnancial security) is collateral to secure a large load customer’s

obligation to reimburse the interconnecting electric utility for rate base eligible Upgrade Costs in

the event of certain events occur that trigger that reimbursement obligation, and (2) a CIAC is an

upfront cash payment made by large load customer for the Direct Costs incurred by the

interconnecting electric utility.




7
  Most TDUs use the term “facility extension agreement,” because that is the term used in their tariﬀs for
interconnecting loads to the power grid. However, since ERCOT’s Planning Guide and PURA § 37.0561 use the term
“interconnection” rather than “facility extension,” CenterPoint Energy’s proposed alternative rule 25.194 uses that
term.

                                                        8
        The Company believes that the ﬁnancial security should cover all “rate base-eligible costs”

incurred by the interconnecting electric utility to establish the large load interconnection. The

Company’s alternative rule deﬁnes rate base-eligible costs as interconnection costs that the

interconnecting utility determines are eligible for recovery through rates approved by the

commission in a future ratemaking proceeding. Further, in order to reduce risk that costs may be

borne by other ERCOT customers, the Company believes that the Commission could require the

interconnection agreement to obligate the large load customer to reimburse the utility for its rate

base-eligible costs if the large load customer either prematurely cancels their interconnection

agreement or the commission disallows the rate base-eligible costs in the future ratemaking

proceeding.

       The required CIAC should therefore cover all non-rate base-eligible costs incurred by the

interconnecting electric utility to establish a large load customer’s interconnection to the ERCOT

grid. Under an interconnection agreement, the large load customer would be obligated to pay

the CIAC before the interconnecting electric utility incurs any interconnection costs or it must

provide a security for the CIAC if it is to be paid after the interconnection is completed.

                                           CONCLUSION

       CenterPoint Energy appreciates the Commission Staﬀ’s request for comment on its

discussion draft and looks forward to developing a rule that balances all the competing needs and

interests of the parties in the ERCOT market.



                                                      Respectfully submitted,

                                                      ____________________________________
                                                      Mickey Moon

                                                  9
      Associate General Counsel
     State Bar No. 00791291
     1111 Louisiana Street
     Houston, Texas 77002
     mickey.moon@centerpointenergy.com
     (713) 207-7231 (office)
     (832) 314-6551 (cell)

     ATTORNEY FOR CENTERPOINT ENERGY
     HOUSTON ELECTRIC, LLC

                                       EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

•   CenterPoint Energy believes the Commission should update the pro forma Retail Delivery Tariﬀ

    that is part of rule 25.214(d), to incorporate the large load interconnection process that is

    ultimately adopted in this Project.

•   CenterPoint Energy also believes that the Commission’s rate ﬁling package (the “RFP”) adopted

    under 22.243(b) should be updated, speciﬁcally, that RFP Schedule M-3.2 should be split into two

    parts: one part for only large load customer interconnection projects for which a customer CIAC

    was required, and a second part that for all other transmission projects for which a customer CIAC

    was required.

•   There are two general categories of interconnection costs incurred by an electric utility to

    interconnect a load customer: (1) “Direct Costs,” which are the costs incurred by an electric utility

    to purchase and construct the new transmission facilities that are necessary to deliver power from

    the ERCOT transmission system to the load customer; and (2) “Upgrade Costs,” which are the costs

    incurred by an electric utility to install or upgrade certain equipment on the existing transmission

    system that are necessary to maintain the reliability of the existing transmission system.

        o   Direct Costs are non-rate base eligible and should be paid by the interconnecting load

            customer as a CIAC.

        o   Upgrade Costs are rate base-eligible and should be recoverable through rates.

•   An interconnecting load customer should be obligated to pay the Upgrade Costs if (1) the

    interconnecting load customer cancels the load interconnection project after the electric utility

    has incurred Upgrade Costs, or (2) the Commission disallows the electric utility’s request in a

    ratemaking proceeding to recover the Upgrade Costs in rates.

        o   The electric utility should be allowed to secure this contingent obligation by requiring a

            ﬁnancial security for the Upgrade Costs from the interconnecting load customer.


                                                11
 •   A single interconnection agreement between a large load customer and an interconnecting

    electric utility is superior to the Discussion Draft’s dual agreements: a discretionary services

    agreement and an intermediate agreement.

•   The ﬁnancial commitment required by PURA § 37.0561(h) can be either a “security” or a

    “contribution in aid of construction” or CIAC.

•   The ﬁnancial security should cover all “rate base-eligible costs” incurred by the interconnecting

    electric utility.

•   The CIAC should cover all non-rate base-eligible costs incurred by the interconnecting electric

    utility.




                                                12
                       CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule


§25.194. Large Load Interconnection Standards.

(a)   Purpose and Scope. This section sets forth the standards and criteria for an electric utility,

      including a municipally owned utility and electric cooperative, to interconnect a large load

      customer to the ERCOT transmission network.

(b)   Definitions. The following words and terms, when used in this section, have the following

      meanings unless the context indicates otherwise:

      (1)    Backup generating facilities -- Generation facilities that are not capable of

             exporting energy to the ERCOT transmission system and that, in aggregate, can

             serve at least 50% of on-site contracted peak demand based on the aggregate

             nameplate capacity of the generation facilities.

      (2)    Contracted peak demand – The total peak demand that a large load customer

             requests that an interconnecting electric utility serve at a site as stated in an

             executed interconnection agreement.

      (3)    End-use customer -- The legal entity that eventually will consume the electricity

             for its operations at the site subject to an interconnection request.

      (4)    ERCOT large load interconnection study process – The processes and

             requirements adopted by ERCOT for conducting large load interconnection studies.

      (5)    Interconnection costs – The total capital costs, including rate base-eligible costs,

             incurred by an interconnecting electric utility for the engineering, procurement, and

             construction of the transmission facilities and upgrades necessary to interconnect

             and serve a large load customer with and from the ERCOT transmission system,

             and which will be included in the interconnecting electric utility’s rate filing

             package Schedule M-3.2 in a future ratemaking proceeding.




                                               13
                 CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule


(6)    Interconnecting electric utility -- The electric utility, municipally owned utility,

       or electric cooperative that owns and operates the facilities necessary to

       interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission network.

(7)    Interconnection agreement -- An agreement between a large load customer and

       interconnecting electric utility pursuant to subsection (f) of this section that sets

       forth the parties’ respective rights and responsibilities for the interconnection of the

       large load customer’s facilities to the ERCOT transmission network.

(8)    Large load customer -- A customer requesting a new or expanded interconnection

       where the customer’s total peak demand at a single site is equal to or exceeds 75

       megawatts (MW).

(9)    Large load interconnection study -- A set of studies required by ERCOT to

       determine compliance with ERCOT planning requirements and the scope of

       upgrades to existing facilities or new facilities needed to serve a large load customer

       requesting interconnection.

(10)   Project developer -- An entity that develops a real estate site and that is not the

       end-use customer as defined in this section.

(11)   Rate base-eligible costs – Interconnection costs that the interconnecting electric

       utility determines are eligible for recovery through rates approved by the

       commission in a future ratemaking proceeding pursuant to 16 TAC § 25.231(c)(2).

(12)   Requested peak demand -- The total peak demand that a large load customer

       requests that an interconnecting electric utility serve at a site, prior to executing and

       securitizing an interconnection agreement.




                                          14
                         CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule


      (13)   Study agreement – An agreement between a large load customer and

             interconnecting electric utility pursuant to subsection (d) of this section setting forth

             the scope of and fee for the large load interconnection study to be conducted by the

             interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT pursuant to subsection (e) of this

             section.

(c)   Large load customer interconnection requests.               A large load customer seeking

      interconnection to the ERCOT transmission network must submit an interconnection

      request to the appropriate interconnecting electric utility. An interconnection request will

      not be considered complete until the interconnecting electric utility receives the following

      disclosures from the large load customer requesting interconnection.

      (1)    Project developer or end-use customer. A large load customer must disclose to

             the interconnecting utility whether the customer is a project developer or an end -

             use customer.

      (2)    Site control and location. A large load customer must describe the location of the

             proposed load and demonstrate site control for the proposed load location through

             provision of one of the following property interests to the interconnecting electric

             utility:

             (A)        a legally binding option to purchase or lease for the proposed load location;

             (B)        a signed and executed lease agreement for the proposed load location; or

             (C)        a deed for the proposed load location.

      (3)    Substantially similar interconnection request.           A large load customer must

             disclose to the interconnecting electric utility whether the customer is pursuing a

             substantially similar interconnection request for electric service, the approval of




                                                 15
               CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule


      which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing

      the interconnection request.

      (A)     A large load customer that is pursuing a substantially similar

             interconnection request for electric service, the approval of which would

             result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or withdrawing the

             interconnection request, must disclose the following information to the

             interconnecting electric utility:

             (i)     the location, including the load zone, of the substantially similar

                     interconnection request;

             (ii)    the size of the substantially similar interconnection request;

             (iii)   the anticipated energization date of the substantially similar

                     interconnection request; and

             (iv)    the interconnecting electric utility for the substantially similar

                     interconnection request.

      (B)    A large load customer that discloses a substantially similar interconnection

             request under this subsection may anonymize competitively sensitive

             details in its disclosure to the interconnecting electric utility.

      (C)    An interconnecting electric utility must not sell, share, or disclose

             information submitted to the utility under this paragraph (3) other than a

             disclosure to the commission or ERCOT.

(4)   Requested Peak demand.            A large load customer must disclose to the

      interconnecting electric utility the total requested peak demand of the load to be




                                        16
               CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule


      served by the interconnecting electric utility, expressed in MW and megavolt-

      ampere reactive (MVAr) units.

(5)   Schedule for phased energization of requested peak demand. A large load

      customer must disclose to the interconnecting electric utility the expected schedule,

      including the month and year, for phased energization of the requested peak

      demand expressed in MW and MVAr units.

(6)   Site-related studies and engineering services. A large load customer must submit

      to the interconnecting electric utility the large load customer’s plans, expected

      timing, and progress for site-related studies and engineering services required for

      project development before energization (e.g., water, wastewater, or gas). The

      submission must be accompanied by an attestation by an officer or official with

      binding authority over the large load customer attesting that the information

      contained in the submission is complete and accurate at the time the attestation is

      signed. A large load customer must provide updates or progress reports to the

      interconnecting electric utility when requested.

(7)   State and local regulatory approvals. A large load customer must submit to the

      interconnecting electric utility the large load customer’s plans, expected timing, and

      current progress for obtaining state and local regulatory approvals required for

      development before energization (e.g., water, air, or backup generation permits, or

      city or county building permits). The submission must be accompanied by an

      attestation by an officer or official with binding authority over the large load

      customer attesting that the information contained in the submission is complete and




                                        17
                 CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule


       accurate at the time the attestation is signed. A large load customer must provide

       updates or progress reports to the interconnecting electric utility when requested.

(8)    Backup generating facilities.           A large load customer must disclose to the

       interconnecting electric utility whether the customer plans to have on-site backup

       generating facilities. If the large load customer plans to have on-site backup

       generating facilities, the large load customer must also disclose the following

       information:

       (A)     the number of backup generating facilities;

       (B)     the nameplate capacity of each of the backup generating facilities;

       (C)     the fuel source and operational characteristics of each of the backup

               generating facilities; and

       (D)     how quickly each of the large load customer’s backup generating facilities

               can turn on to begin serving the load.

(9)    Dynamic modeling. A large load customer must provide a dynamic load model to

       the interconnecting electric utility.

(10)   Load characteristics and other information.            A large load customer must

       disclose to the interconnecting electric utility the load characteristics (e.g., motor

       type, etc.), load profile (e.g., summer/winter peaking, day/night peaking), and any

       other information about the load reasonably requested by the interconnecting

       electric utility.

(11)   Notification of Changes. A large load customer must notify the interconnecting

       electric utility of any change to the information disclosed under this subsection (c)

       within 5 days of the change.




                                            18
                       CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule


(d)   Large load interconnection study agreement and fee. Within 60 days after receiving

      notice from the interconnecting electric utility that the interconnection request is complete,

      the large load customer requesting interconnection to the ERCOT transmission network

      must execute and deliver a study agreement and pay the study fee described in this

      subsection prior to the commencement of the large load interconnection study. Failure to

      execute a study agreement or pay the applicable study fee before the end of that 60-day

      period may be treated as a withdrawal of the interconnection request.

      (1)    A large load customer with contracted peak demand that is equal to 75MW and less

             than 250MW must pay a study fee not less than $114,000 to the interconnecting

             electric utility for transmission studies performed by the interconnecting electric

             utility and ERCOT. If the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT’s combined

             costs to conduct the large load interconnection study fee is expected to exceed

             $114,000, the large load customer must pay a study fee in the amount of the

             interconnecting electric utility’s and ERCOT’s expected costs to conduct the large

             load interconnection study.

      (2)    A large load customer with contracted peak demand that is equal to or greater than

             250 MW must pay a study fee not less than $314,000. If the interconnecting electric

             utility and ERCOT’s combined costs to conduct the large load interconnection

             study fee is expected to exceed $314,000, the large load customer must pay a study

             fee in the amount of the interconnecting electric utility’s and ERCOT’s expected

             costs to conduct the large load interconnection study.

      (3)    Beginning in 2027, the commission will adjust the values under this subsection on

             January 1 of each calendar year.




                                                19
                        CenterPoint Energy Alternative Proposed Rule

the actual interconnection agreements that the Company has historically used for large load

        The financial commitment required by PURA § 37.0561(h) can be either a "security" or a

"contribution in aid of construction" or CIAC. As set out in the Company's proposed alternative

rule 25.194, (1) a security (or financial security) is collateral to secure a large load customer's

upfront cash payment made by large load customer for the Direct Costs incurred by the

interconnecting electric utility.
